head: Surfshark DNS shutting down on 24 November: switch your DNS servers
dek: Surfshark is retiring its free public DNS service from 24 November 2026, according to its support page. Anyone who typed its DNS addresses into a phone, computer or router should move to another resolver.
details: The service used the addresses 194.169.169.169 (IPv4) and 2a09:a707:169:: (IPv6). Surfshark's page names Google or Cloudflare as resolvers to switch to. TechRadar reports the service ran for about 19 months and that Surfshark cited limited adoption.
where: Everyone who set Surfshark's public DNS by hand, from 24 November 2026
means: If your phone, computer or router uses 194.169.169.169 as its DNS server, websites may stop loading once the service is retired.
todo: Check your device's or router's DNS settings. If you see 194.169.169.169 or 2a09:a707:169::, replace them with another resolver, for example Google's or Cloudflare's, before 24 November.
